chunks: And from him (Al-Shaykh) from Ali ibn Ibrahim ibn Hashim from Hammad ibn Isa from Hariz from Zurarah and Ibn Muslim, Zurarah said:

I said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him): 'If there is more than one in the city (i.e., multiple eligible recipients of Zakat)?' He said, 'Give them all, if you are able.' He then said, 'It is not permissible for one who has forty dirhams upon which the year has passed to take it (for himself), and if he takes it, he takes it as forbidden (Haram).'

key_terms.أَرْبَعُونَ دِرْهَماً: Forty dirhams, representing the Nisab (minimum threshold) for silver in this context
key_terms.الْمِصْر: The city or town where the recipients are located
key_terms.يَحُولُ عَلَيْهَا الْحَوْلُ: The year has passed (lunar year) over the wealth

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on distributing Zakat to multiple recipients and can the owner take the Zakat amount for themselves?
ai.summary: Zurarah and Ibn Muslim inquire with Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) regarding the distribution of Zakat among multiple eligible recipients in the same city, to which the Imam advises giving to all if one has the means. He further clarifies the ruling for the owner of Zakat wealth (Nisab), stating that if the owner takes the Zakat amount for themselves, it is considered Haram (forbidden). This highlights the principle of avoiding double-dipping when the giver is also eligible, a key nuance in Shia fiqh regarding Zakat distribution.
